Also, stocks age differently; for many film stocks, magenta is the hardiest color and the last to fade, so many photographs will have a pink/purple tinge to the photograph. A lot of this color fading and color shifts we have come to interpret as "vintage," and we often associate it with the decade.

TL;DR - Different film stocks and lenses become popular in different decades, so photographs from a specific decade will often have a specific "look" that we commonly see with other photos from the era.
